args: How is packet_info.private_table owned, initialized, and destroyed across packet dissection, particularly for wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-rtps.c dissect_rtps? Are entries conventionally allocated with GLib allocation when the table has g_free key/value destructors, and is replacing the RTPS_TCPMAP_DOMAIN_ID_KEY_STR entry expected?

The reported ASan double-free occurs because dissect_rtps at wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-rtps.c lines 11930-11938 creates pinfo->private_table via g_hash_table_new_full(g_str_hash, g_str_equal, g_free, g_free), but allocates the inserted key and endpoint_guid value with wmem_strdup/wmem_memdup from wmem_packet_scope(). A second RTPS header under the same packet replaces the constant-key entry, invoking g_free on the old wmem value, after which packet-scope cleanup frees it again. I am considering changing these inserted allocations to g_strdup and g_memdup2 (or g_malloc plus memcpy), matching the hash table destructors, and want to verify lifecycle and compatibility conventions.
